en: And even before Saikal’s many daughters-in-law
Could look back toward their village,
We suffered misery and innocent deaths,
Though our livestock had grazed freely,
And men despaired of life.
The cause of their despair
Was an army vast as a hearth-fire,
Which devastated the people without respite.
A tyrant named Sarybay arose,
Gathering the people and mustering an army,
Amassing the entire host in abundance.
When his khan gave the command,
He stiffened and poured out his fury,
And while he stood enraged,
Could the Saruu voice any grievance?
When your lord bellows from his throne,
Is there a horse among the people that a camel could stop?
Not a single head of livestock remained in the pens,
Nor strength remained to turn and flee,
Not a shod yearling remained,
Not a living soul among the born remained.
He began such outrages,
And anyone who resisted
He slaughtered without leaving one alive.
He committed notorious atrocities,
And brought every mortal low.
Seizing his moment, he scattered us,
Raging and shouting,
Bringing calamity upon mankind,
Sarybay drove us here.
When he carried out his massacre,
Saying, ‘Do as I command,’
Sarybay brought us as his chosen force.
The black halter of the fugitives
Sarybay brought concealed.
Our precious heads into calamity
Sarybay brought entangled.
While the people lived in freedom,
Hunting deer when they grew weary,
And when they were not weary, the dear people
Delighting in great festivities,
Sharing joy together,
While many peoples lived happily,
He brought such strife upon the nation,
And revealed horrors never seen by man.
The warriors’ misery boiled over,
As though struck by a plague of turmoil,
He drove souls onward without rest.
The infidel son of an ogre
Was seized by his thirst for blood.
He ruined the nation and corrupted the people,
Starting conflict and breaking the army,
Humiliating the entire nation
And oppressing all the people,
Destroying all that had been completed,
And leaving even resourceful men
Helplessly ruined.
For every hundred men, one man
Was appointed chief and drove them on.
Thus the dear people were oppressed,
And their misery boiled over.
Please hear the people’s grievance;
We have no inheritance left to divide.
Restrain your anger.
You fought the desperate Sarybay
And struck him down,
Laying him flat upon his back.
This tiny host has committed no crime,
And has no strength left to fight.
Will you take us as your own people?
Lion son of the bloodstained warrior,
Will you heed these rightful words?
Do not needlessly massacre
The multitude who have done no wrong;
Spare their spoonful of blood.
If by chance you find them guilty,
Then, hero, slaughter them if you must.
But if the rumor spoken is true,
On the dreadful Day of Judgment
We shall make the ogre’s infidel son
A scapegoat, saying, ‘He slaughtered the innocent,
And committed this outrage.’
So shall we bear witness against him.
Strike us fiercely if you will;
Without count and without recourse,
We have fallen into your hands today.
Take us as your own people.
Do not descend to Sarybay’s level
And inflict grievous conflict upon us.
Do not slaughter all together
The dear people who bear no guilt.
You will pass beyond a bloodstained hand,
And reach the farthest bounds of the nation;
It would betray supreme fairness and justice,
Hero, if you failed to show them now.
When your noble bearing leads us,
Reveal the mark of kingship.
Great trials run in your blood;
Spare the spoonful of blood
Of these guiltless people, hero.
Because of what has happened,
We gathered as a people,
Driven here by force,
Bound without cord or rope,
Our eyes darting in bewilderment.
For every thousand men, one
Was appointed as chief.
All our affliction was thus:
Those remarkable men who heeded no counsel,
The meek who understood nothing,
Those who plowed grain to sustain life,
And cut hay in preparation for winter,
Young and old alike,
He drove away the entire people.
He bound burdens upon their backs
And threw this nation into distress,
Beginning a terrible conflict.
Pouring out his wrath, Sarybay
Slaughtered them utterly.”
So spoke the people amid their clamor,
And the host cried out in uproar.
Before the descendant of the noble lion,
They submitted to brave Seytek,
And spoke before the people.
The heroes serving as mediators,
Resourceful champions,
Men who whetted their sharp tongues
And spoke eloquently before khans,
The most skillful spearmen,
The strongest of the assembled host,
Men who had seen much,
And wise, eloquent counselors,
Stood with hands folded.
Changdayak, the army’s finest,
Said this to brave Seytek:
“If you are a hero and a lion,
Your first ancestor was Tügöl Khan,
Blessed from the beginning by Khydyr,
Descendant of the primal hero,
Heir to the first holy man.
Sarybay was your enemy;
Do not regard everyone as a foe.
Sarybay was the swine,
So, hero, do not cast your terrible venom upon us.
Hero, you need living souls to tend,
And a hero such as you
Needs a people such as us.
We shall sell our coursers and pay tribute;
Sarybay was the one you opposed.
If you seek vengeance upon Sarybay,
Descendant of the blessed lion,
If you charge in wrath,
Draw your sword from its sheath
And unleash your dreadful fury.
Slaughter us all.
If your daily rage seizes you,
Gouge out our eyes in vengeance.
We are Sarybay’s countless host,
A people ravaged by war.
Here and now,
We are sheep fallen into your hands.
We turn our warhorses’ heads,
Hoping you will shelter us like a poplar.
Here in front of you, Changdayak and all,
We stand with folded hands.
We are captives in your hands,
All of us accounted guilty.
If you are truly a khan,
Do not assail our precious lives,
But let us go safe and sound.
Sire, since you are our khan,
Draw your sword from its sheath.
Without sparing a single soul,
Slaughter us all.
If you ask of former times,
We are men from the Windy Pass;
Beginning struggle, conflict, and strife,
Hero, we came here to fight.
But now, brave Seytek,
We are mortals fallen into your hands.
We bow our heads to truth,
Hoping mercy will come from the hero,
And ask you for one spoonful of blood,
Too little even to fill your mouth.
As a seven-day trust,
Hero, we beg you for our lives.
If you spare us and leave us alive,
Our poplar trees will become standards,
Our knives will be whetted,
Whatever we gain we shall share together,
Companions sharing every endeavor.
Our red tongues speak eloquently;
You, river-maned lion, must decide.
Look with favor upon the innocent people.
If a gathered nation flees,
Its abandoned livestock rots at bare stakes,
Yet while it endures, a people sustains life.
The guilt for this conflict is upon my hands;
Now, gray-maned lion, we stand
In your hands, my hero.
We lie within the iron cage
Of the iron-armored gray-maned lion.
Having encountered the bloodstained warrior,
Hero, we stand within your grasp.
We have entered the flames of hell
And stand amid its embers.
From your fathers and forefathers
None ever yielded to an enemy,
No mortal who faced them prevailed,
No man could withstand their coming.
They say fortune favors the worthy,
Yet when you look within,
They say the face of the earth is broad.
How many have come lamenting,
How much wealth is there,
How much lies in the treasury?
Every soul begs for its spoonful of blood;
Understand this, noble gray-maned lion.
We are captives fallen into your hands;
I renounce defiance—hero, heed my words.
Your first ancestor was Manas Khan,
Whose yurt walls were anointed with fat.
When men such as us fell into his hands,
He made them khans throughout the lands.
He enriched the lattice walls of their yurts,
And when they fell to him as plunder,
Your champion ancestor Manas Khan
Made them khans throughout the lands.
If you are a hero and a lion,
If you are Manas’s heir in times of trial,
May you spare us,
The common folk now in your hands.
If surging wrath seizes you,
You may slaughter us all.
You will come upon us without turning aside;
If your fierce fury begins,
Then commence the massacre.
A hero needs a people;
Leave our lives intact,
Hero, act according to your will.
Livestock and souls need land,
And you, hero, need a people,
A broad nation of common folk.
Know that this is what I say;
Generous sultan, heed my words.
Heed them and leave us alive;
If you do not, slaughter us.
We stand with lives held in trust,
Amid the embers of your judgment;
If you fire your gun, we are your bullets,
If you kindle a blaze, we are your fire.
Amid conflict and calamity,
We are trapped upon the road,
In a net from which no struggling frees us.
We are in so deep a pit, hero,
That no winged creature could escape.
